A thousand kilometres from the infernos gorging on northern Ontario’s boreal forests, Erin O’Connor watched the sky above Canada’s biggest city turn an “almost post-apocalyptic” orange as it filled with light-scattering particles of soot and ash. Stepping outside the halls of Toronto General hospital, where air filters were keeping patients safe from the worst of the fumes, she was struck by a smell so strong it felt like standing by a campfire.

“It really hit you in the face as soon as you walked outside,” said O’Connor, who runs University Health Network’s emergency department and saw a rise in patients presenting with allergies and shortness of breath. “As the days progressed, it was like that everywhere. It seemed even inside you could smell that burning.”

items.title: La même crise à Ceuta dans un monde différent
items.content_html:
Le grand sage a dit Hispano-arabe Averroès que « la véritable amitié ne se mesure pas aux intérêts temporels, mais s'enivre d'amour gratuit ». Pour le philosophe andalou, les voisins doivent s’unir, non pas par simple commodité économique, mais par une authentique volonté de poursuivre le bien commun. C'est peut-être l'absence la plus éloquente de relations entre l'Espagne et le Maroc, et par extension entre l'Europe et sa frontière sud. Le dernier crise à Ceuta le démontre avec une cruauté insupportable : plus de 80 jeunes morts, dont beaucoup encore non identifiés ; des familles qui continuent désespérément à chercher leurs proches ; des milliers de mineurs abandonnés à leur sort. Tel est le bilan honteux de cette tragédie.

items.title: German Chancellor Merz completes cabinet reshuffle
items.content_html: After days of confusion, Chancellor Friedrich Merz has reshuffled his cabinet. Conservative politicians fear that this will not help with the prospects in the upcoming state elections.

items.title: Germany: Islamist terror attack on Berlin Pride parade triggers political debate
items.content_html: Following the terrorist attack on Berlin's Pride parade, the Christopher Street Day parade, politicians and security experts are demanding consequences.

items.title: 'Amnesia' about measles risk and low vaccination rates have helped US infections grow
items.content_html: The latest US data show measles cases from January to mid-July 2026 totaled more than all cases in 2025. Experts blame a fall in vaccination and warn that people have forgotten measles can be life-threatening.

items.title: FIFA boss Infantino takes aim at World Cup critics
items.content_html: In a strongly worded open statement, FIFA President Gianni Infantino has hit out at those he says were too "consumed by hate and criticism" to enjoy the tournament. Infantino brushed off a number of corruption concerns.

items.title: Car ramming attacks: Why do they keep happening?
items.content_html: Cars are being used as weapons, to ram, kill and maim innocent people. The reasons why are not always clear, nor are solutions to preventing such attacks.

items.title: Berlin Pride ramming: Police shoot suspect dead
items.content_html: Police said the suspect was shot dead in an operation, after the incident was classified as an "Islamist terrorist" attack. One person was killed and several others injured in the attack.

items.title: WAFCON 2026: What you need to know
items.content_html: Several months after it was supposed to start and with more teams than first planned, WAFCON 2026 is finally set to begin. The hosts want a maiden title while a tournament outsider have one of its best players.

items.title: Lenacapavir will slow HIV infections if there's enough of it and it reaches at-risk groups
items.content_html: Lenacapavir is one injection, twice a year. It's a big improvement for people in high-risk groups, currently taking a pill a day against HIV infection. But its long-term impact depends on it reaching those very people.

items.title: Tour de France final stage shortened due to wildfires
items.content_html: Security personnel assigned to the race have been redeployed to help contain major blazes near Bordeaux, reducing Sunday's final stage.

items.title: Eco wins: Cities, creatures, and tech are saving the day
items.content_html: From an AI-powered cute little pangolin, heat mapping to cool down cities and animals reducing wildfire risks by doing their thing, these real-world climate hacks are helping communities stay ahead of a changing planet.

items.title: Highs and lows as Bayreuth Festival turns 150
items.content_html: The Bayreuth Festival's 150th anniversary has been clouded by controversy surrounding German-Jewish speaker Michel Friedman. Yet it offers an opportunity to celebrate, including with an AI-enhanced Ring cycle.

items.title: Why Trump's 'forced labor' tariffs leave the world puzzled
items.content_html: After the US Supreme Court struck down Donald Trump's emergency tariffs, the White House has turned to another trade law linked to alleged human rights abuses.

items.title: The trees helping fires spread and what to do about it‌
items.content_html: With Spain declaring an emergency, France seeking EU help and Canada dealing with more than 900 hot spots, wildfires are out of control. Monocultures and climate change are partly to blame but can we stop the burning?

items.title: How vanilla's history is not so … 'vanilla'
items.content_html: Long before "vanilla" meant bland, the bean's fandom spanned Mesoamerican elites to European courts. But it owes its ubiquity to a 12-year-old enslaved boy.

items.title: Jürgen Klopp and Germany: A partnership long in the making
items.content_html: In one of the worst-kept secrets in football, the former Dortmund and Liverpool boss has been named head coach of the German men's national team.

items.title: Klopp named new head coach of Germany men's football team
items.content_html: Germany has turned to Jürgen Klopp to lead a new era for the four-time world champions after their disappointing World Cup exit, with hopes of building toward future international tournaments.

items.title: Spain's solar eclipse trilogy: spectacle starting August 12
items.content_html: From August 2026 to January 2028, amateur and pro sky watchers are in for a series of rare solar spectacles over Spain and North Africa. Astronomers expect the events to attract millions from around the world.

items.title: ECB keeps interest rates unchanged amid Iran war inflation
items.content_html: The European Central Bank has kept its base interest rates steady but said it was "closely monitoring" the energy price shock. The impact of the war against Iran on energy costs has pushed inflation over ECB targets.

items.title: Oil prices jump as Hormuz, Red Sea crises deepen
items.content_html: Renewed strikes on shipping in the Gulf and the Red Sea have dealt a fresh double blow to global oil markets, with the price of crude oil once again passing $100 a barrel. DW examines what could push prices even higher.

items.title: US citizens are ramping up pressure on data centers
items.content_html: Rapid data center construction across the US, fueled by AI, comes with serious threats to the environment, public health and energy supply. Local opposition has blocked or delayed dozens of projects.

items.title: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
items.content_html: China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

items.title: Female coaches want more representation in African football
items.content_html: Female head coaches will be a rare sight at the Women’s African Cup of Nations. However, there are some promising signs.

items.title: Will surge in German business bankruptcies hit growth?
items.content_html: Company insolvencies in Germany are rising sharply. Is this a sign of deeper economic weakness, or just a market correction that could ultimately benefit future growth?

items.title: Austria turns Hitler's birthplace into police station
items.content_html: The house where Adolf Hitler was born in 1889 is now a police station. Austrian authorities have long sought to prevent it becoming a neo-Nazi pilgrimage site.

items.title: Can VR help you achieve your goals?
items.content_html: A Max Planck researcher has developed VR and smartphone tools that let you "meet" your future self. The science behind it is more powerful than it sounds.

items.title: 'Antifa' song climbs to top of charts after TV show cancellation
items.content_html: German rapper Danger Dan and pianist Igor Levit had been invited to play a song for the 100th episode of a political satire show on TV. The performance was canceled at the last minute due to its message.

items.title: Why the youth jobs crisis is becoming global
items.content_html: Young people in much of the world face growing competition for entry-level jobs as graduate numbers rise, hiring slows and AI-driven disruption adds uncertainty to career prospects.

items.title: How heat waves are messing with your sleep
items.content_html: Residents across Europe have struggled to sleep during the latest record heat waves. But as the planet continues to warm, sleep deprivation could create an epidemic of mental and physical ill-health.

items.title: England and Liverpool football legend Kevin Keegan dies aged 75
items.content_html: English former striker and manager Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75 after a battle with cancer. He was a two-time European footballer of the year with Hamburg.

items.title: How 'blue dot fever' is affecting concerts
items.content_html: Live music remains popular, but many concerts are struggling with unsold tickets and cancellations. While superstars fill stadiums, smaller venues and acts are facing a crisis.

items.title: Taking stock of 2026 World Cup: Football's biggest show yet
items.content_html: A worthy world champion, a call from the US president, security concerns and a few pleasant surprises: The biggest World Cup ever is now over. So what will we remember about the 2026 World Cup?

items.title: Spain wins second World Cup after beating Argentina in final
items.content_html: After a 16-year wait, Spain has claimed a second men's World Cup. Ferran Torres scored the winner in a deserved 1-0 victory over Argentina, which means Spain is now men's and women's world champions.

items.title: New Bundesliga TV deal in US prioritizes reach over money
items.content_html: The Bundesliga has a new home on American screens after Germany's top football league left ESPN. The new deal is a sign of the times.

items.title: Cities are getting smarter about water and other eco wins
items.content_html: From flood-resistant infrastructure to new ways of securing drinking water, cities are adapting to the growing climate pressures of a hotter, drier world. Plus, tourists pitching in to help sea turtles.

items.title: The EU climate policy the world copied is under fire — what's at stake?
items.content_html: The EU Commission has proposed to weaken Europe's emissions trading system, a global blueprint for pricing carbon and cutting CO2. How effective is the scheme and where does it fall short?

items.title: How AI and satellites help fight wildfires
items.content_html: Wildfires are raging across Europe, Canada and beyond. To successfully fight these fires, speed is essential. A German startup uses satellite data and AI to spot fires early.

items.title: Iran's oil supply threat extends beyond Strait of Hormuz
items.content_html: Oil and gas producers in the Gulf are seeking alternatives to the Strait of Hormuz as traffic again comes under fire. But is Iran also turning its attention to the pipelines meant to bypass the waterway?

items.title: US slaps 25% tariffs on Brazil with election looming
items.content_html: The US will impose a 25% tariff on most imports from Brazil starting later this month. It's the first action in the Trump administration's new tariff strategy, after the Supreme Court struck down its prior impositions.

items.title: AI: Why Europe is falling behind, and how it can catch up
items.content_html: Europe trails the US and China in artificial intelligence. Economist and Nobel laureate Philippe Aghion says better research funding, venture capital and AI innovation can help it catch up.

items.title: Will gold prices extend their record-breaking run?
items.content_html: Predictions suggest the price of the precious metal will keep hitting new record highs as investors seek a safe bet in turbulent times. Some forecasts say prices could double within five years.

items.title: East-West border death zone now Germany's biodiversity oasis
items.content_html: Many endangered species now live in the area that once formed the border between East and West Germany. Environment Minister Carsten Schneider recently visited the "Green Belt," and DW went along for the ride.

items.title: Could Russia be about to lose its grip on chess leadership?
items.content_html: Russians have long pulled the strings when it comes to the governing body of international chess. But now two Germans are vying for FIDE's top job.

items.title: England vs. Argentina: A football rivalry full of history
items.content_html: From the Falkland Islands to Diego Maradona and David Beckham, there is so much history between the two 2026 World Cup semifinalists.

items.title: Running dry: How to store more groundwater for dry seasons
items.content_html: More frequent weather extremes are leading to water shortages during droughts and flooding during heavy rain. But groundwater storage can help secure water for dry seasons while mitigating extreme rain.

items.title: Why Indonesia's economy is under pressure
items.content_html: Southeast Asia's largest economy risks losing its emerging-market status as President Prabowo Subianto's spending plans rattle markets. Can he deliver growth?

items.title: 150 years of the Bayreuth Festival: Confronting a troubled legacy
items.content_html: Should the past be confronted — or avoided? Why the Wagner festival's handling of its Nazi-era legacy remains a contentious issue in its 150th anniversary year.

items.title: T. rex 'Gus' sells for record-breaking $50.1 million
items.content_html: The Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton surpassed its pre-sale estimate and set a new auction record for a dinosaur fossil.

items.title: Micronutrients are good, a balanced diet is better
items.content_html: Chronic illnesses, heart disease, obesity ― we know eating too much of the wrong foods can be unhealthy. But what about "good" foods: Is modern farming diluting micronutrients in our fruit and vegetables?

items.title: Germany's Ahr Valley: Rebuilding better after deadly flood
items.content_html: New walls, redesigned bridges and restored floodplains: Towns in a small German valley are testing how they can survive the next extreme flood.

items.title: Are German companies leaving the country?
items.content_html: Should I stay or should I go? Given Germany's high cost and sluggish growth, some business leaders are mulling relocating, or at least investing abroad. DW has a look at the numbers.

items.title: California's largest lake is turning to dust
items.content_html: The Salton Sea is drying up, worsening air pollution for nearby communities. Officials are racing to contain it, but for some families, it's already too late.

items.title: Heat is especially hard on people taking antidepressants
items.content_html: High temperatures can increase the risk of dizziness, dehydration, exhaustion and other heat-related problems for people taking antidepressants.

items.title: When London stank to high heaven
items.content_html: In 1858, London sweltered through an unbearable heat wave. The River Thames reeked so badly it left people gasping for air. "The Great Stink" went down in history — and ultimately gave London a modern sewer system.

items.title: Vegan pregnancy tests and other eco wins this week
items.content_html: Keeping cool in the heat with a millennia-old tradition in India, a German company making animal-free medical tests, and building from bottles in Mozambique.
